description: IMAGE, the International Monitor for Auroral Geomagnetic Effects, is a network of ground magnetometers coordinated by the Finnish Meteorological Institute. The pages read on 2026-09-28 describe 53 stations maintained by 10 institutes from Finland, Germany, Norway, Poland, Russia, Sweden, Denmark and Iceland, spanning geographic latitudes 51 to 82 degrees from Svalbard and Greenland to central Europe, with a station table giving coordinates, provider and operating dates back to the 1982 EISCAT magnetometer cross. Users can view real-time and last-30-day preliminary data, fetch monthly files, and download data for a chosen period and station set, averaged from 10 seconds up to one hour, with wget instructions; derived products include the IL, IU and IE electrojet indicators and equivalent current maps. Coverage is Fennoscandia, Svalbard, Iceland and Greenland, and parts of northern Europe. Access is free: the rules of the road declare an open access policy for scientific use with a required acknowledgement, and no formal licence is named. Caveats: recent data are preliminary, station sets change over time, and the file formats were not inspected. It supports space weather studies of power grids, such as estimating geomagnetically induced currents in Nordic transmission networks during a storm. Related records: SuperMAG, the IRF Kiruna observatory and NOAA geoelectric storm simulations.
